But it supports the yen and adds upward pressure on front-end JGB yields, especially with USD/JPY near 160. articles.title: ICYMI: Fed’s Jefferson says inflation is the key signal for rates, with PCE still at 3.6%
articles.expand: Jefferson’s comments support pricing for a December hike without adding to the half-point tail, which suits the steady, gradual camp. By naming energy as the main channel for broader inflation, he makes Fed expectations sensitive to oil. Any renewed jump in crude tied to the Iran war and Hormuz shipping risk would feed quickly into rate pricing and the US dollar. His upbeat view on growth and jobs also removes an easy reason to pause. That keeps front-end Treasury yields supported, and continues to put gold under pressure from the Fed’s tightening path. --- With unemployment steady and growth ...

articles.expand: Knot’s line on fiscal discipline matters most for euro zone sovereign spreads, especially French bonds against German Bunds. Markets will read it as a reminder that ECB support would be conditional rather than open-ended. A president with that view could make investors less willing to bet on a full central bank backstop if French finances get worse, which risks wider spreads during periods of stress. A smooth departure for China would close the story, but an unexplained delay or cancellation would quickly become a factor for markets. articles.expand: An explicit signal from the Bundesbank president that further tightening is likely should support the euro and push up short-dated euro zone yields, especially German two-year debt. Because he ties the risk directly to gas and electricity, euro zone rate pricing is now more sensitive to moves in energy markets, so a rise in oil or gas could feed quickly into ECB hike expectations. His comment that the economy has proved resilient also weakens the argument that growth worries will hold the ECB back, which leaves rate-sensitive European equities more exposed. --- Not only open mouths at the ECB:...

articles.title: Weekend Fed speak: Collins backs steady, gradual rate hikes, cool on a bigger December move
articles.expand: Collins’s comments push back on the half-point talk that has built since Waller’s remarks and last week’s inflation data. That could trim some of the tail pricing for a larger December move and take a little heat out of the front end of the Treasury curve. Her view that the eventual rate path may be higher cuts the other way, though. It supports the idea of a longer hiking cycle, which keeps the US dollar supported on dips and leaves gold without a clear dovish tailwind. articles.title: Aino Bunge: Interest rates should be adjusted gradually in an uncertain situation
articles.expand: “The Swedish economy is recovering on a broad front, and inflation is expected to rise above target next year. This development justifies a tighter monetary policy, and it is likely that interest rates will be raised further over the coming year. However, any future increases must take into account, not least households’, sensitivity to interest rates." These comments were made by First Deputy Governor Aino Bunge, speaking at Swedbank about the Executive Board’s decision to raise the policy rate to 2 per cent.
